questions.presentation: A 30-year-old male patient with no medical history except smoking presented to the emergency department with nausea, dyspnea, and malaise for the past seven days. On presentation, the patient was hypoxic, tachycardic, and febrile to 103 degrees Fahrenheit. Chest radiography at the time showed large right lower lobe opacities (Figure 1). Labs showed hyponatremia with a sodium of 123 mmol/L (normal 135-148 mmol/L), hypokalemia of 2.9 mmol/L (normal 3.3-5.1 mmol/L), leukocytosis of 14.0 k/mm3 (normal 5.0-10.0 k/mm3), and borderline elevated lactic acid of 2.6 mmol/L (normal 0.7-2.5 mmol/L). An electrocardiogram was concerning for S-T elevation, and cardiology was consulted. The troponin measured was negative at <0.01 ng/mL (normal 0.0-0.1 ng/mL), and cardiology suspected pericarditis after a repeat electrocardiogram.

questions.presentation: A previously healthy 46-year-old man presented to emergency department with a 2-day history of cough and high-grade fever. On the morning of presentation, he had developed sudden onset shortness of breath while at rest. He had a history of cigarette smoking for 4 months before the development of symptoms. He initially smoked two to three cigarettes on weekends when with friends but had been smoking three to four cigarettes on a daily basis for the last few weeks. He had no previous history of asthma, atopy or illicit drug use. He denied being exposed to any animals, birds or livestock. He had not travelled during the last one year and denied being exposed to chemical fumes. On admission, vitals were as follows: blood pressure of 110/88 mm Hg, pulse of 100/min and respiratory rate of 18/min. He was noted to have SpO2 of 75% on room air which improved to 91% on 10 L of oxygen via nasal cannula.

questions.presentation: A 56-year-old man presented with vague abdominal pain, fullness in the right iliac fossa, and gross as well as microscopic hematuria for 20 days. The post-transplantation course was uneventful. The patient maintained stable renal allograft function with serum creatinine around 1 mg/dL and had no rejection episodes. Initially, every six months and later every year periodic ultrasonography and doppler imaging were conducted that had been unremarkable during these 13 years. On evaluation with ultrasound, a heterogeneous vascular mass sized 9.0x7.3x6.8 cm was seen involving the upper pole of the renal allograft (Fig 1). On local examination, multiple erythematous and hemorrhagic papulonodular lesions were present over the extensor aspect of the right arm, extending to include an area of 8 x 6 cm (Figure 1).

name: 胸部影像诊断
description: 肺结节、肺炎、肺结核、纵隔病变等

questions.stem: 男，63 岁，长期吸烟。CT 示右肺上叶 2.8cm 结节，边缘分叶、短毛刺，伴胸膜凹陷。最可能的诊断是：
questions.explanation: 分叶征、毛刺征、胸膜凹陷征是周围型肺癌的典型征象，结合高龄与长期吸烟史，首先考虑周围型肺癌。

questions.stem: 以下哪些征象支持继发性肺结核的诊断？

options.text: 病灶好发于上叶尖后段
渗出、增殖、钙化病灶共存
病灶仅位于下叶基底段

questions.explanation: 继发性肺结核好发于上叶尖后段及下叶背段，常见多形性病灶共存，树芽征提示支气管播散。

questions.stem: 支气管充气征只见于大叶性肺炎，可作为其特异性诊断依据。
questions.explanation: 支气管充气征见于多种肺实变性病变（如肺炎、浸润性黏液腺癌、淋巴瘤等），并不特异。

name: 腹部影像诊断
description: 肝胆胰脾、胃肠道、急腹症等

questions.stem: 乙肝肝硬化患者，增强 CT 示肝内肿块动脉期明显强化、门脉期廓清。该强化方式通常描述为：
questions.explanation: 肝细胞癌主要由肝动脉供血，典型表现为动脉期明显强化、门脉期/延迟期廓清，即“快进快出”。

questions.stem: 超声诊断急性阑尾炎时，提示阳性的阑尾外径一般大于：
questions.explanation: 阑尾外径 >6mm 且加压不可压缩，是急性阑尾炎常用的超声诊断标准。

questions.stem: 阑尾腔内粪石是阑尾穿孔的高危因素之一。
questions.explanation: 粪石可导致阑尾腔梗阻、压力升高，增加坏疽和穿孔风险。

name: 神经影像诊断
description: 脑血管病、颅内肿瘤、脱髓鞘病变等

questions.stem: 急性脑梗死在 MRI 上最早出现异常的序列通常是：
questions.explanation: 细胞毒性水肿导致水分子扩散受限，DWI 在发病数分钟至数小时内即可呈高信号，ADC 值降低。

questions.stem: 提示颅内病变位于脑外的征象包括：

options.text: 病灶与脑组织间存在脑脊液间隙
病灶周围白质指状水肿且位于脑实质内

questions.explanation: 宽基底、白质塌陷征、脑脊液裂隙征均为脑外肿瘤的定位征象；D 项提示脑内病变。

questions.stem: “脑膜尾征”是脑膜瘤的特异性征象，出现即可确诊。
questions.explanation: 脑膜尾征常见于脑膜瘤，但也可见于转移瘤、淋巴瘤等，不具特异性。
